title: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900)

intro.about: Microsoft Certified: Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900) validates foundational knowledge of cloud concepts and of Azure itself: what moving to the cloud changes about cost, resilience and responsibility, which Azure services do which jobs, and how an Azure estate is managed and governed. The study guide current as of July 20, 2026 defines three skill areas: Describe cloud concepts (25-30%), Describe Azure architecture and services (35-40%), and Describe Azure management and governance (30-35%).
intro.audience: Built for people demonstrating foundational Azure knowledge: newcomers to cloud entering technical roles, sales, procurement, finance and project professionals who need to discuss Azure credibly, students, and administrators or developers formalising fundamentals before role-based certifications. The exam's verb is describe, never configure — every question here tests recognition, discrimination between neighbouring services and terms, and appropriate-use judgment, not portal steps, syntax or SKU tables.

materials.title: 50-question practice form
materials.description: Weighted to the published skill-area bands (28/38/34 after band-midpoint normalisation) and drawn from a 65-item originally-authored bank in which every one of the current outline's 57 objective bullets is represented. Microsoft publishes a 40-60 question band rather than an exact count; this mock models 50.

materials.title: Three question formats, with disclosed approximations
materials.description: Mostly four-option single choice, plus choose-two multiple-response items and scenario-matching items that approximate the real exam's hot area and drag-and-drop types. Microsoft deliberately does not publish its exam's format list; the format coverage note below carries the full mapping and what is not rehearsed here.

materials.title: Review dashboard and rationales
materials.description: Per-domain scoring against a 70% bar — an honest proxy for the real exam's scaled 700-of-1,000 pass mark, which Microsoft warns may not equal 70% of the points — plus an explanation for the key and every distractor on submission, phrased in the study guide's own vocabulary.

intro.disclaimer: An independent, originally-authored study tool for personal exam preparation — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Microsoft Corporation or Pearson VUE. "Microsoft", "Azure", "Microsoft Entra", "Microsoft Purview" and "Microsoft Certified: Azure Fundamentals" are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. Every question was written clean-room from documented derivation artefacts against the public study guide, with prior practice material analysed for classification only, exactly as this package's derivation records. Nothing here is drawn from the live AZ-900 item bank: real exam content is confidential and protected by the Microsoft Certification exam agreement, which binds you too once you sit the exam — please never share live questions here.

format_coverage: Microsoft does not publish the item types used on a given exam ("To protect exam security and the value of our certifications, we don't identify specific exam formats or question types before the exam"). What it does publish is the sample list demoed in its exam sandbox — multiple choice, drag and drop, hot area, build list, active screen and case studies (labs do not apply to Fundamentals exams) — plus confirmation that "problem-solution question sets" exist, where one scenario is restated with a different proposed solution and answered Yes or No. This mock supports three formats and approximates as follows. Multiple choice maps exactly to single_choice (four options). The problem-solution shape's judgment — does this proposal actually satisfy the stated requirement? — is exercised inside standard four-option single-choice items, but neither its two-option Yes/No mechanic nor the series relationship (one scenario restated with different proposed solutions) is reproduced. Multi-select multiple choice maps to multiple_response (choose two of five). Drag and drop is approximated by scenario_matching. Hot area (a grid of statements each answered independently) is approximated by all-or-nothing multiple_response, which loses the per-statement No branch. Build list (place steps in order) is approximated by single_choice over candidate orderings. Active screen (configure a control in a rendered interface) and case studies (several dependent items under one shared scenario) are not represented at all; their underlying concepts are authored as standalone items. Two scoring divergences are disclosed alongside: the real exam awards partial credit on multi-part items (one point per correctly answered component) where this mock's multiple_response is all-or-nothing, and the real exam reports a scaled 1-1000 score with 700 to pass — which Microsoft states "may not equal 70% of the points" — where this mock reports percent correct against a 70% bar.
